# Annualized return (CAGR) (`cagr`)

*Category: Return summary · Nature: derived · Unit: decimal_return · Formula id: `cagr@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Constant yearly growth rate that would produce the observed cumulative return.

## 2. Formula

```text
(prod(1 + r_t))^(P / n) - 1, where P = periods per year and n = observations
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns with a regular frequency.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Higher is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

The average yearly growth rate, taking compounding and losses into account.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Geometric mean return annualized with the canonical periods-per-year factor; the standard GIPS-style annualized return. Always below the annualized arithmetic mean when returns vary.

## 7. Assumptions

- Observation frequency is correctly established.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- The history is shorter than one year: annualizing extrapolates a partial year (GIPS prohibits presenting annualized returns for periods under one year).
- The history contains missing periods.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

One observation mathematically; low confidence below 3 years. (policy `location`: Mean-type estimates: low confidence below 3 years, moderate below 5 years.)

## 10. Reference implementations

| Library | Function | Agrees | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| PerformanceAnalytics 2.0.4 (R) | `Return.annualized(geometric=TRUE)` | yes |  |
| empyrical-reloaded 0.5.12 | `annual_return` | yes |  |
| QuantStats 0.0.81 | `stats.cagr(periods=12)` | yes | Agrees when periods=12 is passed for monthly data; the default (periods=252) treats every observation as a trading day. |

## 11. Sources

- Bacon, C. R. (2021). Practical Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement (2nd ed.). Wiley.
- CFA Institute (2020). Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) for Firms, provisions on annualized returns. <https://www.gipsstandards.org/>

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

Observation count (not calendar span) with the canonical periods-per-year factor (decision 0004).
